lesson_title: Read Your Phone Like a Passport
hook_text: Your phone crossed six borders before it reached your pocket. Check its stamps.
clip_script: Start with your phone, and read it the way a detective reads a passport. The design was drawn in America or Korea. The processor chip was etched in Taiwan. The screen glass was melted in Korea or Japan. The battery holds cobalt from the DRC and lithium that may have left Zimbabwe. Assembly happened in China, Vietnam or, increasingly, India. And last night's software update reached you through an undersea cable that comes ashore at Melkbosstrand on the West Coast. Six countries, minimum, folded into one object in your pocket — and your takkies could tell the same story: designed on one continent, stitched on a second, shipped through a third, sold to you on a fourth. That is globalisation, worn daily.
visual_style: A passport flipping open with border stamps appearing for each phone component; parts drifting to their countries on a rotating globe; the final stamp thudding down as a cable surfaces from the Atlantic onto the West Coast.
mood: Detective-story curiosity landing on a sharp everyday realisation.
pacing: Stamp-by-stamp rhythm, quickening through the components, then a slow reveal for the undersea cable coming home.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson: the two doors that built the one-world shop, who wins, who loses, and where South Africa stands.
